title: Cell drill closes on any Escape anywhere on the page
body:
## Summary
CellDrillPanel listens for Escape on `document`, so an Escape meant for another surface (a select, the CLI terminal, a modal) also closes the drill.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CrossModuleFeatureDashboard/CellDrillPanel.tsx:120 registers a document-level keydown that calls onClose for every Escape, regardless of focus or defaultPrevented. Fixed looks like: ignore events with defaultPrevented, or scope the listener to focus within the drill / the heatmap.

## Flow
- open a drill by clicking a status count
- focus another control that uses Escape (sort select, terminal input, a Modal)
- press Escape -> the drill closes as well

## Expected impact
Operators working in the drill stop losing it to unrelated Escapes. Could break: users who rely on Escape from anywhere to dismiss it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Escape only dismisses the drill when it is meant for the drill
Before: 1 document-level listener, no defaultPrevented or focus check (walked)
After: predicted: 0 closes when Escape is consumed elsewhere
Method: simulation - walked the listener; no component test exercises a competing Escape consumer
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: render dashboard + a sibling input whose keydown calls preventDefault on Escape; assert drill stays open (red before, green after)

title: 'msvc-version' error category has no producer
body:
## Summary
CATEGORY_LABELS in src/lib/prompt-context.ts:241 labels a 'msvc-version' category that ErrorCategory does not contain and no fingerprint rule emits.

## Description
src/types/error-memory.ts:5 ErrorCategory has 12 members, without 'msvc-version'; src/lib/error-fingerprint.ts:15 CATEGORY_PATTERNS never emits it. This round removed the same key from ErrorMemoryPanel's severity map (now Record<ErrorCategory, ...>). The prompt-context label map is still Record<string, string> and carries it. Fixed: type CATEGORY_LABELS as Record<ErrorCategory, string> and drop the key, or add the category to the fingerprinter if MSVC version errors are meant to be caught.

## Flow
- grep msvc-version src -> only prompt-context.ts:241 (and formerly ErrorMemoryPanel)
- type CATEGORY_LABELS by ErrorCategory
- typecheck flags the excess key -> remove or add a producer

## Expected impact
One vocabulary for error categories across the fingerprinter, the prompt and the dashboard. Could break: legacy DB rows labelled msvc-version (none can exist, no producer).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one category vocabulary, typed
Before: 1 label for a category with 0 producers; CATEGORY_LABELS untyped by ErrorCategory
After: 0; a new category without a label fails typecheck
Method: probe - grep for producers across src; out of this context (prompt-context belongs to another context)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: typecheck with CATEGORY_LABELS: Record<ErrorCategory, string>; seeded control deletes one key -> 1 error

title: getErrorMemoryStats computes topPatterns that no consumer reads
body:
## Summary
The error-memory stats query runs a sixth SELECT for topPatterns, but the only reader of ErrorMemoryStats (ErrorMemoryPanel) never renders it.

## Description
src/lib/error-memory-db.ts:293 selects top patterns on every get-stats call; grep for topPatterns finds the ErrorMemoryStats type and this query, plus an unrelated crash-health field (src/lib/crash-health/health-map.ts:19). ErrorMemoryPanel.tsx renders totals and topCategories only. Fixed: either render the patterns in the panel (what the agent actually learned) or drop the query.

## Flow
- open Evaluator > Scanner
- POST /api/error-memory get-stats runs 5 queries incl. topPatterns
- panel renders no pattern

## Expected impact
One fewer query per load, or a panel that shows what was learned. Could break: an external consumer of the API field (none found in tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - drop an unread query (or quality - render it)
Before: 5 SELECTs per get-stats, 1 result unread (0 consumers by grep)
After: 4 SELECTs, or 1 rendered list
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep; the file is the database-layer context, owned by a sibling this wave
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn topPatterns src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx (non-test): src/lib/error-memory-db.ts:271,293,304; src/lib/crash-health/health-map.ts:19,73 + CrashHealthMap.tsx (different type)
instrument: unit test on getErrorMemoryStats against a temp DB asserting the returned keys; plus the zero-consumer grep re-run

title: Evaluator child views type onNavigateTab and linkTab as plain string
body:
## Summary
onNavigateTab is (tab: string) => void in DependencyGraph, SessionAnalytics, ProjectHealth and HolisticHealth, and SubsystemSignal.linkTab is string, so a typo compiles.

## Description
src/types/project-health.ts:150 linkTab?: string; src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/OverviewTab.tsx:17 onNavigateTab?: (tab: string) => void. This round added a runtime guard in the shell (d6e58abe) so a bad id no longer crashes, but it now fails silently with a logger.warn. Typing both as EvaluatorTabId moves the failure to compile time.

## Flow
- type linkTab and every onNavigateTab prop as EvaluatorTabId
- remove the shell casts
- typecheck flags any stale id

## Expected impact
A stale drill-link is caught at build, not by an operator clicking a dead card. Could break: callers passing computed strings need a narrowing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - tab ids checked at compile time
Before: 5 string-typed seams (4 props + linkTab); a typo -> 0 type errors
After: 0 string seams; a typo -> 1 type error
Method: probe - read the 5 seams; they sit in 3 other contexts (project-health, holistic-quality, session-analytics)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: typecheck; seeded control sets one health-engine linkTab to an unknown id -> 1 error

title: Zero-count heatmap cells name a generic div
body:
## Summary
Empty status cells render `<div title aria-label>` with no role, a name ARIA prohibits on generic elements, so assistive tech drops it.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CrossModuleFeatureDashboard/HeatmapGrid.tsx:172 puts aria-label on a plain div. ARIA 1.2 prohibits naming role=generic; the row button already announces every count. Fixed: aria-hidden on the empty cell (and drop the title), or give it role="img"/a visually-hidden text if a per-cell name is wanted.

## Flow
- render a module with a 0 count
- inspect the accessibility tree -> the label is not exposed
- the row button label already carries the 0

## Expected impact
Cleaner accessibility tree, no prohibited ARIA. Could break: nothing visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no prohibited aria-label
Before: 1 prohibited aria-label per zero cell (up to 5 per row)
After: 0
Method: simulation - read the markup against the ARIA spec; no axe run in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: axe-core (or a querySelectorAll("div[aria-label]:not([role])") count) over the rendered grid: N before, 0 after

title: Budget preview mixes a pinned en-GB date with a viewer-locale time
body:
## Summary
SpendBudgetPreview formats dates with a hard 'en-GB' locale but the daily reset time with the viewer's locale, so one sentence can mix conventions.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/SpendBudgetPreview.tsx:27 toLocaleDateString('en-GB', ...) vs :89 toLocaleTimeString([], ...). A US viewer reads '3 Sep' next to '07:00 PM'. Fixed: one formatting helper and one locale choice for both (the app's i18n locale, or both viewer-locale).

## Flow
- open Evaluator > Spend with a monthly limit set
- read the pace line and the reset line
- date and time follow different locales

## Expected impact
Consistent date/time copy on the budget guard. Could break: snapshot or text assertions on the date format.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one locale convention per surface
Before: 2 locale choices in 1 component
After: 1
Method: simulation - read both call sites; no test renders under a non-GB locale
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test rendering BudgetPace with Intl default locale stubbed to en-US; assert date and time follow the same locale

title: Error Memory panel hard-codes motion and an amber palette class
body:
## Summary
ErrorMemoryPanel animates bars with a literal 0.4s duration (not MOTION / reduced-motion aware) and paints unresolved counts with raw text-amber-400 instead of a status token.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/ErrorMemoryPanel.tsx:152 transition duration 0.4 (repo convention: MOTION constants from @/lib/constants, motionSafe for reduced motion); :168 text-amber-400 where STATUS_WARNING / SEVERITY_TOKENS are the canonical hue used by the bars two lines up. Fixed: MOTION.slow + the shared reduced-motion helper, and STATUS_WARNING via style.

## Flow
- open Evaluator > Scanner with recorded errors
- bars animate for 0.4s even under prefers-reduced-motion
- unresolved count uses a different amber than the severity bars

## Expected impact
Panel follows the motion and colour conventions. Could break: nothing functional.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - convention sites
Before: 2 off-convention sites (1 motion literal, 1 raw palette class)
After: 0
Method: probe - read and counted in the file
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source scan test (comments stripped) for numeric `duration:` literals and `text-(red|amber|green)-\d+` classes in the file; seeded control

title: Evaluator tab strip lacks Home/End keys
body:
## Summary
The 31-tab strip handles ArrowLeft/ArrowRight only; the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern also expects Home/End, which matter most on a strip this long.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/EvaluatorModule/index.tsx:67 returns early for every key except the two arrows. Reaching the last tab (Wrapped) from Overview takes 30 arrow presses. Fixed: Home focuses+activates the first tab, End the last.

## Flow
- focus the Overview tab
- press End -> nothing happens
- press ArrowRight 30 times to reach Wrapped

## Expected impact
Keyboard users reach the far tabs in 1 key instead of up to 30. Could break: a page-level Home/End handler (none in this shell).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard reach on the tab strip
Before: worst case 30 keypresses to the last tab
After: 1
Method: probe - read the handler and counted tabs (31)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: keyDown End on the active tab -> the last tab is aria-selected (red before, green after)
